method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the paradox of inward freedom and practical responsibility, the several meanings of the world, attention, desire and recognition, images of birds, mirrors, prisons and mirages, the transience of wealth, fame and power, historical addresses in their settings, and the return through prayer and remembrance to kindness, moderation and service. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Beware lest earthly affairs extinguish thee.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: beware lest earthly affairs extinguish thee; a brief closing warning before the guide’s final passage.

selected.text: These people love the immediate and forsake the hereafter.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: these people love the immediate and forsake the hereafter; a memorable brief diagnosis.

selected.text: turn away from the world, for He giveth life while it taketh it away
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: turn away from the world, for He gives life while it takes it away; a concise contrast.

selected.text: No man can be happy without God, though he may not know why he is miserable.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that no one can be happy without God though he may not know why he is miserable; a memorable insight.

selected.text: This earthly realm is one of servitude, pollution, headache and helplessness.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that this earthly realm is servitude, pollution, headache and helplessness; a blunt description.

selected.text: Hath the world prevented you from your Lord, the Lord of Names, or vain desire?
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking whether the world or vain desire has prevented you from your Lord; a direct self-examination.

selected.text: Beware lest the veils of the world and its manifestations and colors prevent you.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning against the veils, manifestations and colors of the world; names its veiling power.

selected.text: Leave the world to its people and hold fast unto the cord of wisdom and utterance.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: leave the world to its people and hold fast to wisdom and utterance; a concise practical counsel.

selected.text: purify them from the defilement of the world and its suspicions and its idle fancies
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking that souls be purified from the defilement of the world and its idle fancies; begins the movement to prayer for purification.

selected.text: Lethargy and coldness have encompassed the world - set aflame the heart of the world!
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: lethargy and coldness have encompassed the world, set aflame its heart; a call to active service.

selected.text: The nobility of the human world lies in divine inspirations, not in worldly adornments.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá locating human nobility in divine inspirations, not worldly adornments; a concise statement of true worth.

selected.text: As long as man is much attached to this world he will be unaware of the Kingdom of God.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that attachment to this world leaves one unaware of the Kingdom; a concise principle.

selected.text: The world hath so deceived them that they see neither right nor left. Lo! They know not.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: the world hath so deceived them that they see neither right nor left; a brief image of blinding deception.

selected.text: Beware lest the ornaments of earthly sovereignty prevent thee from the Kingdom of thy Lord
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning lest the ornaments of earthly sovereignty prevent one from the Kingdom; addresses power.

selected.text: Blessed are they whom these two fleeting days have not debarred from the immortal Kingdom
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing those whom two fleeting days have not debarred from the immortal Kingdom; blessing of the detached.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world hold you back or the clamor of the nations veil you
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning lest worldly affairs or the clamor of the nations veil you; adds public noise to the obstructions.

selected.text: The world and its ornaments have deluded them, and its riches and favors have occupied them
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world’s ornaments, riches and favors have deluded and occupied them; a compact diagnosis.

selected.text: Indulgence in these things make one negligent of God and stifles all traces of spirituality.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that indulgence makes one negligent of God; indulgence and spirituality.

selected.text: Beware lest the world debar you from Him Who created it. Hasten ye unto the Kawthar of grace
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: beware lest the world debar you from its Creator, hasten to the Kawthar of grace; turning to grace.

selected.text: The world is transient - look not unto it, but rather unto Him Who created and manifested it.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: the world is transient, look not unto it but unto Him Who created it; turns attention to the Creator.

selected.text: become independent of the world and all that is therein through the remembrance of thy Friend
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: become independent of the world through remembrance of thy Friend; independence through remembrance.

selected.text: be not of them whom the multiplication of worldly things hath altered and who have turned away
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: be not of them whom the multiplication of worldly things has altered; abundance and change.

selected.text: man leaves this majestic gift and great station to run away and play with the dust of the Earth
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on man leaving his great station to play with the dust of the earth; a vivid contrast of capacity and use.

selected.text: God willing, may they all not be deprived of everlasting gifts on account of transient blessings
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh hoping none be deprived of everlasting gifts on account of transient blessings; transient and everlasting gifts.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world sadden thee and turn thee away from the Lord of all mankind.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning lest the affairs of the world sadden and turn one from the Lord; sadness itself as a distraction.

selected.text: I prayed at the Court of Holiness to deliver thee from the darkness of the attachment to this world
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that the addressee be delivered from the darkness of attachment to this world; follows the mirror image with prayer.

selected.text: All human beings are like children occupied with toys of dust, and their aspirations are very low.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening human beings to children occupied with toys of dust; a brief image of immature aspiration.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world sadden you or its ornaments prevent you from My Straight Path.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning lest the world’s affairs sadden or its ornaments divert from the Straight Path; sadness and ornament together.

selected.text: The sovereignty of this world hath no value, and the glory of this realm of dust hath no permanence.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that worldly sovereignty has no value and its glory no permanence; a concise verdict on power.

selected.text: paid no heed to the comforts and ease of this world, and chosen the other world over this first life
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising one who paid no heed to comforts and chose the other world; a portrait of preference.

selected.text: The world hath deluded them to such extent that they cast aside guidance and took hold of idle fancy
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world deluded people into casting aside guidance for idle fancy; delusion and guidance.

selected.text: turn not unto the world and what is therein, for it shall perish while sovereignty remaineth with God
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: turn not to the world, it shall perish while sovereignty remains with God; enduring sovereignty.

selected.text: they are heedless of God yet alert to the world, asleep to the Kingdom yet awake to the realm of dust!
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on people heedless of God yet awake to the realm of dust; a compact image of misdirected wakefulness.

selected.text: Seek not thy nest in the faded groves of this world nor thy shelter in this dark and dismal wasteland.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: seek not thy nest in the faded groves of this world; the nest image of the bird.

selected.text: The deceptive conditions and allusions of the world have debarred the nations from the most great bounty.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world’s deceptive conditions have debarred the nations from the most great bounty; collective diagnosis.

selected.text: Say: O people! Have ye occupied yourselves with the world and become heedless of the Beloved of the worlds?
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking: have ye occupied yourselves with the world and become heedless of the Beloved; a direct question.

selected.text: They have forsaken their God and followed their own desires. Woe unto them from the torment of a mighty day!
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those who followed their desires and forsook God; brief warning.

selected.text: So the people of Baha attach their hearts to the other world. They seek happiness only from the world above.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the people of Bahá seek happiness only from the world above; orientation of heart.

selected.text: forget this world of possession, become wholly heavenly, become embodied spirit and attain to universal mind
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: forget this world of possession, become wholly heavenly and attain to universal mind; aspiration beyond possession.

selected.text: Another cause was that they were firmly attached to the world. They had not in their hands the Divine Balance.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that attachment to the world left people without the Divine Balance; attachment and judgment.

selected.text: Beware, O My loved ones, lest ye exchange that which ye possess for that which hath been ordained in the worlds.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning loved ones not to exchange what they possess for what is ordained in the worlds; a caution to believers.

selected.text: the world and all that is therein are not worthy of attachment, as that which perisheth deserveth not to be loved
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that what perishes deserves not to be loved; a concise principle of detachment.

selected.text: Turn not your attention to the world and its concerns, but rather turn your hearts toward the abode of the Beloved
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: turn not your attention to the world but your hearts toward the Beloved’s abode; redirecting attention.

selected.text: Beware lest the world prevent you from attaining the presence of God. For this were ye created, did ye but know it.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: beware lest the world prevent you from attaining God’s presence, for this were ye created; purpose of creation.

selected.text: that they may not grovel all the time in the world of matter and that they may not only think of eating and drinking
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping people may not grovel in matter or think only of eating and drinking; brief practical hope.

selected.text: Thou must do always something and speak in such a manner that the people's attachment to this world may become less.
selected.reason: Reported advice of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to act and speak so that people’s attachment to the world may lessen; a distinctive practical application.

selected.text: The greatest cause and mightiest reason was the love of the world, which prevented those souls from the Lord of Names
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that love of the world was the greatest cause preventing souls from the Lord of Names; a root cause.

selected.text: Yet most of the men and women servants have been veiled by earthly troubles, selfish desires, and the dust of passion.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that servants are veiled by earthly troubles, selfish desires and the dust of passion; adds troubles to desires.

selected.text: Woe unto those who are veiled by what they possess from what God possesseth - they are truly among the perishing ones.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: woe to those veiled by what they possess from what God possesses; possession as veil.

selected.text: The idol of self and desire hath encompassed the world. All have turned away from God and become worshippers of desire.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the idol of self and desire has encompassed the world; desire as rival worship.

selected.text: Cast aside the world and take hold of that which the Lord of Eternity, Who is in the Most Great Prison, commandeth thee.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: cast aside the world and take hold of what the Lord in the Most Great Prison commands; a command from prison.

selected.text: The material men of this world are like poison to the spiritual … others are like swine, which eat everything they find
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that material men are like poison to the spiritual; a sharp warning about company.

selected.text: if you wish to deliver yourself from evil ones and from all harm, leave the world to its people and never draw near to it
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: leave the world to its people and never draw near it, to be delivered from harm; protection through detachment.

selected.text: Know thou that the world is the love of Mine enemies and the turning away from My sanctified, luminous and beloved Beauty.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh defining the world as love of His enemies and turning from His Beauty; a further definition of the world.

selected.text: The secrets of the whole economic question are divine in nature, and are concerned with the world of the heart and spirit.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that the secrets of the economic question are divine and concern the heart and spirit; joins material problems to the life of the spirit.

selected.text: Be not content with the world of nature, but seek the glory of the Kingdom, for this is the greatest gift among all peoples
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: be not content with the world of nature but seek the glory of the Kingdom; a direct counsel beyond natural existence.

selected.text: Let not earthly affairs grieve thee. Rejoice in My remembrance of thee and My turning towards thee from this forbidden spot.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: let not earthly affairs grieve thee, rejoice in My remembrance of thee; a personal turn from grief to remembrance.

selected.text: But alas, some hearts became attached to the earthly world and remained veiled and deprived of those favors and assistances.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on hearts attached to the earthly world that remained deprived of divine favors; consequence of attachment.

selected.text: How base must a person be to be content with these material things and to occupy and soil oneself with these superfluities.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to one asking for money on the baseness of contentment with superfluities; a practical application.

selected.text: closed thine eyes to the ease and comfort of this fleeting world and to the praise of the inmates of this gloomy heap of dust
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising one who closed his eyes to the ease and praise of this fleeting world; detachment from praise.

selected.text: Leave the world behind you, turning unto God, the Forgiving, the Generous. That which ye possess will profit you not this day.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: leave the world behind, what ye possess will profit you not this day; possessions and the Day.

selected.text: All have sullied themselves with these conditions and are drowned in the world of nature, heedless of God and the higher realm
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on people drowned in the world of nature and heedless of the higher realm; diagnosis in brief.

selected.text: I am occupied with the mention of this sorrowful world; bestow upon me an ear that may hear the melody of the Concourse on High
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying for an ear to hear the Concourse on High amid this sorrowful world; prayer for wider attention.

selected.text: I am tired of going about looking at the things of this world. I want to go above and travel and see in the spiritual worlds
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to a museum watchman, tired of looking at things of this world and wishing to see spiritual worlds; a distinctive anecdote.

selected.text: Say: O people! Are ye content with this vain life while turning away from the dominion of immortality in the presence of Beauty?
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking whether people are content with this vain life while turning from immortality; contentment questioned.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world hold thee back. Leave them behind thee and turn with thy heart to the Most Sublime Horizon.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: leave worldly affairs behind and turn with the heart to the Most Sublime Horizon; turning of heart.

selected.text: They have occupied themselves with the world, turning aside from Him Who is the Lord of the Throne above and of the earth below.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those occupied with the world and turned from the Lord of the Throne; brief diagnosis.

selected.text: But the love of the world and its concerns hath so seized them all that no awareness remaineth for anyone, save whom God willeth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that love of the world has so seized all that no awareness remains; the scope of attachment.

selected.text: It is most astonishing that they would deprive themselves of the eternal, everlasting Kingdom for the sake of this transient life.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: most astonishing that they forfeit the eternal Kingdom for this transient life; astonishment at the choice.

selected.text: If today one should conquer the whole world, he hath not been nor shall he be, in the sight of God, powerful and triumphant
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that one who conquers the whole world is not powerful in the sight of God; separates conquest from true triumph.

selected.text: all have turned away from the eternal stations for the sake of this ephemeral world and remained deprived of their ultimate purpose
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that all have turned from eternal stations for an ephemeral world; loss of purpose.

selected.text: But for one whose entire attention is focused on this world--and this world is in the utmost difficulty--what can gladden his heart?
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking what can gladden the heart of one whose attention is focused on a troubled world; attention and joy.

selected.text: They have cast aside the Lord and seized upon their desires. Thus have their souls enticed them, and today they are among the dead.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that those who seized their desires are today among the dead; desire as spiritual death.

selected.text: These weak souls who have the utmost attachment to this transient world - it is certainly better if they are not in the Cause of God.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that souls utterly attached to the world had better not be in the Cause; a sober qualification about commitment.

selected.text: Otherwise, woe and misery to the soul that seeketh after comforts, riches, and earthly delights while neglecting to call God to mind!
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Grieve not over this world and its conditions. Rather, rejoice in this remembrance, which all the treasures of the earth cannot equal.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: rejoice in this remembrance, which all the treasures of the earth cannot equal; remembrance beyond treasure.

selected.text: glory be unto the handmaiden who hath turned with her heart unto the Lord of the Last and the First and hath left the world behind her
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh glorifying a handmaiden who turned to the Lord and left the world behind; a woman’s example of detachment.

selected.text: By My life! They have not found the sweetness of this station and are pleased and occupied with the ornaments and things of the world.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those who have not tasted the sweetness of this station and are pleased with things of the world; contrasting sweetness.

selected.text: In these brief days of earthly life do not contaminate thyself with the embellishments, the comforts and the aspirations of this world.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: in these brief days do not contaminate thyself with the world’s embellishments; brevity and purity.

selected.text: riches and hopes have deprived the servants from the All-Possessing, the Self-Subsisting, and from the outpourings of this wondrous Day
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that riches and hopes have deprived servants of the All-Possessing; hopes as attachment.

selected.text: Thou dost not look to the world. … By God! My servants who have turned with radiant countenance toward the All-Merciful have divorced it
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that servants turned to the All-Merciful have divorced the world; a decisive image.

selected.text: Every wise person will not rest his affections on the comfort and joys of temporary life. At all times one should seek the eternal truth.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the wise rest not their affections on temporary joys; wisdom and the eternal.

selected.text: Cast the kingdom behind thee, then turn unto thy Lord. The world and all that is therein shall perish, and sovereignty shall remain with God
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Hell is the state of mind in which there are evil thoughts and purposes, yielding to the desires of the senses, clinging to material things.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá defining hell as evil purposes, yielding to the senses and clinging to material things; a definition of the inward state.

selected.text: Verily, he who sucketh from the breast of the world hath turned away from God, the Lord of Names … Turn not unto the world and its conditions
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that he who sucks from the breast of the world has turned from God; a distinctive image of dependence.

selected.text: Nor is this fleeting life of such worth that it should distract any soul from the True One or deflect him from that which is pleasing unto Him.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Be not saddened by the transient affairs of this base world. Keep thy heart illumined and joyous through the remembrance of the King of Oneness.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: be not saddened by transient affairs, keep the heart joyous through remembrance; joins joy and remembrance.

selected.text: The splendor from Us be upon you and upon those whom the affairs of creation have not prevented from turning to the Lord of the Day of Judgment
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing those whom the affairs of creation have not prevented from turning to the Lord; blessing the free.

selected.text: For the sake of two days of transient life they forsook everlasting life, and for ephemeral bounties they closed their eyes to eternal blessings
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that for two days of transient life people forsook everlasting life; transience and loss.

selected.text: Beware lest what hath been created on earth prevent you from attaining unto the station whose decree hath been inscribed in the Preserved Tablet
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh lest what is created on earth prevent attaining one’s inscribed station; destiny and creation.

selected.text: Is the king free as the bird is free to fly upward? The king's head is often heavy with anxiety and the things of this world which hold him down.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking whether a king is as free as a bird, his head heavy with worldly anxiety; sets outward sovereignty beside inward freedom.

selected.text: The world hath deluded most of the servants. Blessed is he who hath cast it behind him, turning with his heart to the direction of the Intended One.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing him who casts the deluding world behind him and turns to the Intended One; the possibility of turning.

selected.text: Worldly affairs should be left to worldly people. Grasp the hem of the eternal form, gird up your loins firmly, and forget sovereignty and kingdom.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: leave worldly affairs to worldly people and forget sovereignty and kingdom; a direct counsel.

selected.text: That sovereignty is earthly and not the intended meaning, for earthly sovereignty ultimately leads to "the loss of both this world and the Hereafter
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that earthly sovereignty leads to loss of this world and the Hereafter; clarifies the meaning of sovereignty.

selected.text: The centers around which the thought of the majority of mankind revolve are egoism, selfishness, blind passion, hypocrisy, insincerity and cupidity.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming egoism, selfishness, passion, hypocrisy and cupidity as the centres of most human thought; a blunt diagnosis.

selected.text: They have taken the vain imagining and cast aside the Self-Subsisting. To this doth the Sovereign of Utterance bear witness in this Forbidden Station.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those who took vain imagining and cast aside the Self-Subsisting; imagining against reality.

selected.text: Be content with God and independent of him who waxed proud and was wretched, and chose this world over the next by following his passions and desires
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: be content with God and independent of him who chose this world by following his passions; contentment in God.

selected.text: Say: Do ye rejoice in what ye possess while ye behold its passing? Leave it and turn unto the Countenance. This, verily, is the Goal, did ye but know.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking whether people rejoice in possessions while seeing them pass; the Goal beyond possession.

selected.text: Better for you is what He possesseth than the things ye yourselves possess and the things ye have sought and are now seeking in this vain and empty life
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Detach thyself from all else but God, thy Lord, then turn thy face toward the sanctuary of His love and good-pleasure, and be of them that are detached.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: detach thyself from all else but God and be of them that are detached; a direct call to detachment.

selected.text: These conditions of madness which are occupation with the affairs of this base world deserve to be forgotten and are worthy of abandonment at all times.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that occupation with this base world is a madness to be forgotten; a strong judgment.

selected.text: Rejoice not in the world and whatsoever it contains. By God's life! Every treasure hath been and is the cause of infinite grief and sorrow and regret
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that every treasure has been the cause of infinite grief and regret; the cost of treasure.

selected.text: Riches have occupied them, turning them away from their final end, and vain imaginings have prevented them from God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that riches have occupied people and turned them from their final end; wealth and purpose.

selected.text: Fear not the might of ignorant divines, and be not gladdened by worldly wealth. Soon shall God's irrevocable decree seize both and bring them to naught.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: fear not the might of divines and be not gladdened by wealth, for God’s decree shall bring both to naught; wealth and might alike transient.

selected.text: Then I told him really this small, humble cottage is more beautiful and exquisite than the palace of the King. He answered in reality it is so, it is so.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a humble cottage is more beautiful than the King’s palace; a narrative reversal of values.

selected.text: My sister was veiled thereby from the Beloved of creation, choosing for herself the ornaments of the world and turning away from the good-pleasure of God
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on His sister choosing the ornaments of the world over God’s good-pleasure; a personal narrative of worldliness.

selected.text: The intoxication of vain ornaments hath so seized the people that they remain heedless and veiled from this supreme bounty. Soon shall death overtake all.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that intoxication with vain ornaments has made people heedless and death shall soon overtake all; mortality and heedlessness.

selected.text: cut thy attention from the earth; that is, cease to attach thy heart unto this world and seek connection with or attachment to the Kingdom and turn unto God
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining “cut thy attention from the earth” as ceasing to attach the heart and seeking the Kingdom; clarifies detachment.

selected.text: How many a servant hath occupied himself with the world, heedless of its transience, and how many a servant hath forsaken it, turning unto his Ancient Lord!
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh contrasting servants occupied with the world and those who forsake it for their Lord; two paths side by side.

selected.text: How many souls today are occupied with their selfish desires, to such extent that they are wholly veiled from the Truth and deprived of the wine of reunion.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on souls so occupied with selfish desires that they are veiled from the wine of reunion; links desire to loss of nearness.

selected.text: All the people of this city are thinking of commerce and industry and pleasure and entertainment, except for you few who are also thinking of and mentioning God
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that all in the city think of commerce and pleasure except a few who mention God; a historical setting.

selected.text: O peoples of the earth! Fear God and follow not those whom the world hath deluded with its vanities in such wise as to have debarred them from My straight Path.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning the peoples not to follow those whom the world has deluded; a caution about influence.

selected.text: How many a learned one cast the Book of God behind his back, and how many a mystic was seized by the winds of the world and withheld from the Most Exalted Horizon
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on the learned who cast the Book behind them and mystics seized by the winds of the world; shows that learning does not protect from worldliness.

selected.text: The world and the hereafter are two states: if your focus is on God, you are in Paradise, and if your gaze is upon yourself, you are in the Fire and in this world.
selected.reason: The Báb’s statement that the world and the hereafter are two states, Paradise when one focuses on God and the Fire when one gazes on self; an inward definition from the Báb.

selected.text: I wonder how the people can live in such an atmosphere all their lives and be happy, spending their precious time in hunting, and devising new games and pastimes.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wondering how people are happy spending their time hunting and devising pastimes; a practical observation.

selected.text: All have been created for the knowledge of God, yet despite this they remain heedless of Him and occupied with themselves. Soon shall all cry out "Oh, woe unto us!"
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that all were created for the knowledge of God yet remain occupied with themselves; purpose and self-occupation.

selected.text: The Greatest prison is the material world. Prison is antithesis of freedom. Now man is a prisoner of food, of sleep, of comfort and thousand other similar prisons
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that man is a prisoner of food, sleep and comfort; names ordinary dependencies as prisons.

selected.text: Beware lest your present condition prevent you from your ultimate destiny, and lest possessions veil you from the remembrance of your Lord, the Mighty, the Most High.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh lest present condition prevent ultimate destiny and possessions veil remembrance; present and destiny.

selected.text: Among the people is he who is held back by wealth from his final end, and among them is he who is occupied with women, heedless of God, the Lord of the Exalted Throne
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those held back by wealth or by women from their final end; distinct forms of attachment.

selected.text: Those men who, having amassed the vanities and ornaments of the earth, have turned away disdainfully from God -- these have lost both this world and the world to come
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: If you put your efforts into understanding the precepts of the Kingdom instead of into acquiring worldly shares and rights, you will gain perpetual joy and happiness.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to a socialist that understanding the Kingdom’s precepts brings joy beyond worldly shares and rights; a distinctive application.

selected.text: Beware lest the conditions of the world and its ornaments, its favors, its bounties and its colors hold you back from turning unto the Dawning-Place of God's revelation
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh warning lest the world’s ornaments, favors, bounties and colors hold one back from the Dawning-Place; a full list of attractions.

selected.text: occupation with such matters and attention to development and gardens and roses and nightingales and hyacinths keeps one from building spiritual houses and true mansions
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that occupation with gardens, roses and nightingales keeps one from building spiritual mansions; even beauty can distract.

selected.text: Yet most are unaware and have not yet awakened from the slumber of heedlessness. They remain content with this transient world and are deprived of the everlasting bounty.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those not yet awakened from heedlessness and content with the transient world; awakening.

selected.text: In truth, all creation is in torment so that they may not become attached to this world and instead seek comfort and rest in the divine world and pursue heavenly gifts
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that creation is in torment so that souls may not attach themselves to this world; suffering’s purpose.

selected.text: Blessed are they whom the affairs of the world have not prevented from the supreme horizon … This mansion of clay hath no worth, and these earthly temples have no station
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that this mansion of clay has no worth and these earthly temples no station; a judgment on bodily life.

selected.text: He spends his time in the pursuit of Shadowy objects. … When man leaves this world then no relatives, no family, no friends will benefit him. He will leave them all behind
selected.reason: Address of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on pursuing shadowy objects while relatives and friends cannot benefit one after death; the limits of what accompanies us.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world withhold thee from the Lord of all mankind. Hold fast unto Him and place thy trust in Him, for He is verily the Helper, the Succourer.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: hold fast to Him and trust in Him, lest worldly affairs withhold you; trust as remedy.

selected.text: There is no real pleasure in the word and no real happiness. All the earthly pleasures and material enjoyments are but alleviations of pains and an appeasement of troubles
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that earthly pleasures are but alleviations of pain; a distinctive account of pleasure.

selected.text: All the inhabitants of this city are either thinking of industry or wealth or they are chasing after the worldly pleasures. except the few of Baha'is who are thinking of God.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a city’s inhabitants think of industry, wealth and pleasure except a few who think of God; a social setting.

selected.text: The heedless souls who remain in the wilderness of self and desire and have not been guided by the dayspring lights of guidance are accounted as non-existent before the Truth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that heedless souls in the wilderness of self and desire are accounted non-existent before the Truth; turns the inquiry to self.

selected.text: How many a servant hath been prevented by the world from the Lord of Names, and how many a servant hath turned and attained unto the recognition of God, the Lord of the worlds.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh contrasting servants prevented by the world and those who attained recognition; two outcomes.

selected.text: Beware lest the ornaments of the world withhold you from the Lord of all beings. Leave behind what the people possess, clinging fast to God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: leave behind what the people possess, clinging to God; a positive counsel.

selected.text: The world is bewildered, for it is observed that the servants, out of love for two fleeting days, have closed and continue to close their eyes to everlasting, eternal blessings.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that servants close their eyes to eternal blessings out of love for two fleeting days; transience and choice.

selected.text: Say: Are ye content with an hour of this world while depriving yourselves of what hath been ordained for you throughout the duration of God's kingdom? This is naught but error.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh asking whether people are content with an hour of this world while forfeiting the duration of God’s kingdom; an hour against eternity.

selected.text: My handmaiden! Verily My sister desired My presence and claimed My love and recognition, but when worldliness touched her she became occupied with it and turned away from My luminous, resplendent Beauty. She chose the ungodly as a helper for herself instead of God
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on His sister, who claimed His love yet turned away when worldliness touched her; a narrative of attachment overtaking devotion.

selected.text: How strange that some souls, for the sake of the fleeting colors of this world and a life of but two days, have remained deprived of God's eternal bounties and everlasting life.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on souls deprived of eternal bounties for the colors of a two-day life; transience.

selected.text: They have attached their hearts to a handful of dust and sand, and dwell in a dark and gloomy world. They have chosen this transient fireplace and shunned the eternal rose garden
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on those who attach their hearts to dust and choose a transient fireplace over the eternal rose garden; contrasting dwellings.

selected.text: By God's life! Their desires have held them back from God and their wealth hath deluded them from Him Who created them and provided for them unto this blessed, mighty, promised Day.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that desires and wealth have deluded people from Him Who provides for them; wealth and desire as obstacles.

selected.text: Such heedlessness hath seized upon the servants that they have forsaken the imperishable kingdom for the sake of two fleeting days, and are occupied with transgression and wickedness.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on servants forsaking the imperishable kingdom for two fleeting days; heedlessness and transience.

selected.text: The intoxication of perishable ornaments hath prevented the servants from everlasting favors. They have clung to these few fleeting days, and remain heedless of that which is with God.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the intoxication of perishable ornaments has kept servants from everlasting favors; intoxication and ornament.

selected.text: This world's foundation is built upon wind and has no end. One should attend to the affairs of this world only to the extent necessary and spend the remaining time on the Kingdom of God
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that this world’s foundation is built on wind and its affairs should be attended only as necessary; a practical measure of engagement.

selected.text: Likewise reflect upon the baseness of the people of the world - they are occupied with that which they themselves acknowledge to be perishable, and are debarred from the life everlasting.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on people occupied with what they themselves acknowledge to be perishable; sharpens the same question of mortality and practice.

selected.text: Some, because their eyes are afflicted with the ophthalmia of desire, have failed to recognize Him and have contented themselves with this perishable world, passing by the eternal Kingdom.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on eyes afflicted with the ophthalmia of desire that fail to recognize Him; the effect of desire on sight.

selected.text: Say: O people of Baha! Turn not unto the world and its ornaments. By God's life! It shall perish, while your remembrance shall endure in the kingdom of your Lord, the Mighty, the Generous.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: turn not to the world, it shall perish while your remembrance endures; contrasts perishing and enduring.

selected.text: The diverse colors of the world have occupied its people and deprived them of the Supreme Horizon, yet he who possesseth sight is not withheld by worldly affairs from the Most Great Prospect
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world’s diverse colors occupy its people, yet one with sight is not withheld by worldly affairs; shows inward freedom is possible.

selected.text: Pay no heed to the world and set not thy heart upon wealth. Neither lament poverty nor boast of riches, for all these things have come from nothingness and unto nothingness shall they return.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: neither lament poverty nor boast of riches, for all come from and return to nothingness; keeps both from measuring worth.

selected.text: Thou seest, O my God, my Purpose and my Master, that Thy servants are occupied with their riches, heedless through their affairs, and prevented by their veils from recognizing Thy chosen ones
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh lamenting servants occupied with riches and kept by veils from recognizing His chosen ones; prayerful diagnosis.

selected.text: Ponder upon the world and its vicissitudes and changes, that ye may know its station and those who have turned unto it, turning away from that which hath been sent down in Our Preserved Tablet.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Among the people are those whom love of the world has prevented from turning to the Lord of Names, and among them are those who have turned to the Most Exalted Horizon, detached from the worlds
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh contrasting those kept back by love of the world with those detached from the worlds; two responses side by side.

selected.text: the world of existence hath a focus of attention, an object of desire, a beloved and an adored one. One loveth position, another yearneth for a beauty brighter than the moon, one is wholly attached to wealth, and yet another clingeth to the hem of the Lord of Glory
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that every soul has an object of desire, whether position, beauty, wealth or the Lord of Glory; names the competing centres of attention.

selected.text: O you who are turned toward the Kingdom, do not wither from the affairs of the human world. By the breeze from the divine realm, remain ever stirred, fresh and verdant, alive, refined and free.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: do not wither from human affairs but remain fresh, verdant and free; a counsel of inward vitality.

selected.text: Our real happiness is in the Kingdom. Here we seek no happiness, because in this world happiness does not exist
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that real happiness is in the Kingdom and does not exist in this world; a statement on happiness.

selected.text: In the world of existence, whatsoever man desireth deserveth no attachment, for in truth it is a mirage and not water, smoke and not roast meat, waves of vain imaginings and hosts of idle fancies.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that whatever man desires in this world is mirage, not water, smoke, not roast meat; contrasts appearance and nourishment.

selected.text: If the purpose of existence is sensual life and pleasures, then animal and man are equal. Happiness and pleasure are rather the possession of the bird and not those of distressed and sorrowful men.
selected.reason: Public address of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that if existence were sensual pleasure, animal and man would be equal; challenges pleasure as life’s purpose.

selected.text: These fleeting days have deprived most from the everlasting bounty, and the pride of wealth and power hath become an obstacle, and love of ornaments hath veiled their eyes like a severe inflammation.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that pride of wealth and power is an obstacle and love of ornaments veils the eyes like inflammation; wealth, power and sight.

selected.text: We do not want spiritual progress, we do not seek human virtues, and we say "We are wealthy, we need not this bounteous feast. We have a flowing treasure, we want not the trouble of heart and soul."
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá voicing those who say “We are wealthy, we need not this bounteous feast”; wealth set against virtues.

selected.text: the market of sugars is thriving and the confectioners' shops are open, with continuous scattering of sweets. Yet the crows crave bones and the owls desire the insects of ruins. Therefore you, who are a divine Indian parrot, take your share of this refined sugar and partake of this soul-nourishing sweetness
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on crows craving bones while the Indian parrot partakes of refined sugar; a distinctive poetic address on spiritual nourishment.

selected.text: The ornaments of the world of creation have prevented the people of the realm below from turning to the highest horizon. They are occupied with these things and are heedless and veiled from the Truth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the ornaments of creation keep the people below from the highest horizon; ornament as veil.

selected.text: The commercial man awakes with the thought of commerce; the inventor awakes with the thought of his inventions; the banker with the thought of money. But you, when you awake, must at once think of God
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the merchant, inventor and banker wake to their concerns but the believer must at once think of God; a practical test of attention.

selected.text: How can a man attain to the ethereal height of true, solid fame if he chases after the shadows of his own pleasures and lust? Will his spiritual station be equal to the one who followed none of these?
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how one chasing the shadows of pleasure can attain true fame; the fleeting shadow image.

selected.text: Consider the handmaiden who was related [to the Cause], how through vain and illusory words she remained deprived of the court of oneness, and how love of the world held her back from the Lord of Names.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on a related handmaiden held back by vain words and love of the world; a personal example.

selected.text: But that sovereignty retained no glory and that majesty had no lasting grandeur. However, his connection to the Sacred Threshold is an eternal sovereignty that will endure forever and remain steadfast.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting a sovereignty without lasting glory with an eternal connection to the Sacred Threshold; passing majesty and enduring connection.

selected.text: Every mention is on their lips except the mention of God. They entertain every thought except the thought of the Kingdom of God. Every call is being heard in Paris except the call of the world of Light.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Paris that every call is heard except the call of the world of Light; a memorable historical address.

selected.text: The beloved of God must strive to be servants of the Blessed Beauty that they may be pointed to with fingers of acclaim, and they must not attach importance to worldly affairs, for these shall pass away.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the beloved of God should be servants and attach no importance to worldly affairs; service as the measure.

selected.text: O bond slave of the world! Many a dawn hath the breeze of My loving-kindness wafted over thee and found thee upon the bed of heedlessness fast asleep. Bewailing then thy plight it returned whence it came.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Dost thou grieve over this world? It shall pass away, by the Lord of the worlds! Rejoice in My love, which nothing created in all existence can equal. Verily, thy Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: dost thou grieve over this world? It shall pass; rejoice in My love; love set against grief.

selected.text: All of the souls are either occupied in pleasure, play, or united in gathering worldly luxuries, and intoxicated with the melody of the world of nature. But the friends of God have held a heavenly feast
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting souls occupied with pleasure and luxuries with the friends of God at a heavenly feast; contrasting gatherings.

selected.text: Some are of a material inclination, enslaved to the world of nature. Their highest aspiration is to make progress in the material world … The other kind of human beings are those who seek the sublime world
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishing those enslaved to the world of nature from those who seek the sublime world; two kinds of aspiration.

selected.text: The world is that which preventeth men from turning toward God, not what heedless servants have understood it to be. Thus hath it been sent down from the Pen of our Most Glorious Lord in a preserved tablet.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh defining the world as that which prevents turning toward God, not what the heedless suppose; a foundational definition.

selected.text: Just as birds and beasts from morning are thinking of grain and food, likewise these people are constantly preoccupied with the means of livelihood. How absorbed they are! What hopes and what joys they have!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening people preoccupied with livelihood to birds and beasts seeking grain; the image of absorption.

selected.text: The world hath never had, nor hath, any permanence. Soon thou shalt find all who are visible therein and all that exists therein to be non-existent, such that thou shalt see no trace of all that is on earth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world has never had permanence and all on earth will leave no trace; a stark statement of transience.

selected.text: Beware lest the affairs of the world withhold you from your Lord, the Most High, the All-Glorious. Cast them behind you and take what hath been given you from the presence of Him Who causeth the morning to break.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: cast worldly affairs behind you and take what has been given; a positive command.

selected.text: In the same way he must be born from the world of nature so that he may become free from the darkness of the world of nature. This is the second birth. … Man must always strive to have his spirit overcome his body
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the second birth from the world of nature and the spirit overcoming the body; spiritual rebirth in bodily life.

selected.text: Everybody who is thinking of besmearing himself (or herself) with the unreal world and not (attaching himself or herself) to the real, he (or she) is a field of bad character and not that of justice and fairness.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that one besmeared with the unreal world is a field of bad character; links worldliness and conduct.

selected.text: Despite this, the heedless are extinguished and the frozen ones are intoxicated. The materialists are caught in the cold of earthly conditions, and the self-indulgent are pleased and addicted to worldly delights.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on materialists caught in the cold of earthly conditions and the self-indulgent addicted to delights; images of cold and intoxication.

selected.text: It behooveth the people of Baha to die to the world and all that is therein, to be so detached from all earthly things that the inmates of Paradise may inhale from their garment the sweet smelling savor of sanctity
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Every maiden in this universe of life has a leading desire. One longs for wealth, and another for worldly honors, and yet another strives for adornment and decoration, while another yearns for pleasure and comfort.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing maidens each with a leading desire for wealth, honors, adornment or comfort; a personal address on ambition.

selected.text: Do not tarry in this world of scents and colors … For the ease and comfort of this dusty, darksome world is all constraint and contamination. The pleasures and delights of all its affairs are but regret and hardship
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: tarry not in this world of scents and colors, whose pleasures are regret; counsel against lingering.

selected.text: The whole world hath been brought from nothingness into being for the recognition of the Ancient King, yet the pomp and vanities of the world have occupied all and prevented them from turning to the Most Exalted Horizon.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the world was created for recognition of God yet its vanities prevent that recognition; ties purpose and obstruction.

selected.text: O Nadir Muhammad! … Nadir shed the blood of several million people in order to conquer an earthly realm and a worldly domain, and in the end he hastened to the world of dust and took up residence in a narrow and dark grave
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to Nadir Muhammad recalling Nadir, who shed blood to conquer a realm and ended in a narrow grave; a distinctive narrative of conquest.

selected.text: and hast proof of the sublimity of purpose. The eagle soaring to the heights of glory will not make its nest and abode in the branches of this transient and base world of abasement. The whale of the divine sea will not take up residence in a worldly stream, and the lion of the Lord's springtime will not make its dwelling
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the soaring eagle, the whale and the lion will not dwell in the base world; images of powers fitted to a higher realm.

selected.text: The metaphorical world and the visible world are both sheer nothingness, though they appear in the garment of existence. The first is the highwayman of the wayfarers, and the second is the trial of those who have arrived.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that the metaphorical and visible worlds are nothingness, the first a highwayman and the second a trial; a distinctive distinction of meanings.

selected.text: Seeking nearness to the wealthy and the affluent, she turned away from her brother. She sent to the house of the enemy one who was related to the Friend. Beseech God that He may sanctify all from excessive love of the world.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on a woman who turned from her brother to seek nearness to the wealthy, with a prayer against excessive love of the world; a narrative example.

selected.text: When I look upon Paris it seems to me it is like unto a corpse on which creep thousands of worms. These worms climb up and down through the dead, putrid corpse sucking its blood and pleased with its flesh. They do nothing else.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening Paris to a corpse on which worms feed; a stark image within its setting.

selected.text: In this world all people are distracted, but each one is distracted by something different. One is distracted by loved ones, another by endless wealth and riches, another by worldly dominion, and yet another by gardens and orchards.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that each person is distracted by something different, even loved ones and gardens; shows that attachment can fasten on good things.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O God of Names and Creator of heaven, to make me of those whom the world hath not kept back from turning toward Thy most exalted horizon, and whom the ornaments of earth have not prevented from drawing nigh unto Thee
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh to be among those whom the world has not kept back from His horizon; asks for freedom from obstruction.

selected.text: Grieve not over the world and its conditions. Rather, rejoice in this station which hath been praised in the Book. … Glory be upon thee and upon those who have cast away the world and have turned with radiant faces toward this Horizon
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: grieve not over the world but rejoice in this station, and glory upon those who cast it away; joy in detachment.

selected.text: Most people have been consumed by the fire of greed and desire while they perceive it not. Blessed is the soul that hath cast off the garment of greed and departed from the world out of love for God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that most people are consumed by the fire of greed without perceiving it; carries the theme of attachments difficult to recognize in oneself.

selected.text: O the pity! that man attacheth himself to this world and is enamoured with ease and comfort notwithstanding these irresistible woes and many toils and sorrows. What heedlessness! What ignorance! What error! How pitiful, how regrettable!
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that man attaches himself to ease and comfort despite irresistible woes; the irony of attachment.

selected.text: Many people come here in a gala journey. They stop at the best hotels. They come here when they have nothing to fear, they travel in a company of friends and are a gay crowd! They do not realize they are on a pilgrimage to a holy place
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on pilgrims travelling as a gay crowd unaware they are on pilgrimage; worldliness in religious practice.

selected.text: Muhammad, upon him be the Glory of God, has been and continues to be under the gaze of divine favor. God, exalted be His glory, Himself bears witness to his service in the divine path. Most of the friends of Truth, in ages past and present, possessed no earthly treasures, and this has never been and is not now a defect, but rather is a manifest
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh assuring that most friends of Truth possessed no earthly treasures and this is no defect; a personal reassurance about poverty.

selected.text: Thou seest and knowest that Thy servants have been prevented from turning unto Thee and placing their trust in Thee, and the ornaments of the world have so occupied them that they have denied Thy manifestations, Thy proofs and Thy signs.
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh that the ornaments of the world have so occupied servants that they deny His signs; worldliness and denial.

selected.text: What is the dust which obscures the mirror? It is attachment to the world, avarice, envy, love of luxury and comfort, haughtiness and self-desire; this is the dust which prevents reflection of the rays of the Sun of Reality in the mirror.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Be not saddened by the sorrows of the world, nor gladdened by its joy. Neither sorrow nor joy is beloved in the Cause of the Beloved. Joy befitteth him who hath recognized this Revelation, and sorrow him who hath heard of its tribulations.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: be neither saddened by the world’s sorrows nor gladdened by its joy; equanimity in the Cause.

selected.text: Thanks be to God that for each one of the divine freed slaves and the heavenly and dear maid-servants, an indestructible mansion will be erected in the New Kingdom. This mansion will be an everlasting dwelling, an eternal abode and shelter.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising an indestructible mansion in the Kingdom for God’s servants; the enduring dwelling.

selected.text: Some people exert the utmost effort to amass something through lawful or unlawful means to leave for their heirs, unaware that both possessions and heirs shall pass away. No name endures on earth except that which is connected to the Truth.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those who amass for heirs unaware that possessions and heirs pass away; accumulation and inheritance.

selected.text: Some of the people of the earth desire conquest over others; some of them are longing for rest and ease; others desire a high position; some of them desire to become famous; thank God that our desire is for spirituality and for union with God.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá listing desires for conquest, ease, position and fame beside the desire for union with God; compares the aims that direct lives.

selected.text: Observe among the people how they have taken as their object of worship that world whose evanescence all acknowledge and confess, and how they remain debarred and shut out from the true Object of worship and from the rays of the Spiritual Sun.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on people who take as their object of worship a world whose evanescence they confess; examines what is actually worshipped.

selected.text: Night and day they are consumed by the fire of greed and deprived of the light of detachment. With all their soul they strive after wealth and glory, heedless of to whom this wealth shall revert the following day and who shall inherit this glory.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those consumed by greed, heedless of who will inherit their wealth tomorrow; the uncertain inheritance of glory.

selected.text: This transient world of dust befits mere owls of ignorance. This gloomy dust-heap is only worthy of the birds of this mortal plane. The mystic nightingale maketh its home in the divine rose-garden and noble birds dwell in spiritual realms on high.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting owls of the dust-heap with the mystic nightingale of the divine rose-garden; a bird image of attraction.

selected.text: People go to the theatre, amuse themselves with sight-seeing, each intent on his own occupation; they dance, they sing, they play, they make music, they walk, they talk, they are plunged in earthly thoughts, immersed in materiality, neglectful of God.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá during carnival week on people plunged in earthly amusements; a historical setting.

selected.text: Attachment to the world hath debarred the servants from the Lord of Names. Ere long they shall arise in lamentation and weeping, but shall find for themselves neither helper nor protector except if they repent and return unto God, the Mighty, the Kind.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that attachment to the world has debarred the servants, with the door of repentance left open; diagnosis with hope.

selected.text: They possess naught but pure fancy and find no eternal life save utter extinction. They have become slaves to self and remained cut off from the King of Kings; they have become servants of the body and remained heedless and veiled from the Lord of Lords.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on those who have become servants of the body and slaves to self; keeps the body–soul priority in view.

selected.text: Most failed to respond, being occupied with the diverse colors of the world and its glory and riches, and are so entangled that they had not, and have not, time to hearken unto the Word of Truth. Heedless of the immortal Kingdom, they cling to ephemeral hues.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on people too entangled in the world’s colors to hearken to the Word of Truth; preoccupation and hearing.

selected.text: Verily, the people are intoxicated with the wine of their own desires to such an extent that they know not what they utter. They speak as their desires command them and purchase with their souls and their wealth the wrath of God, yet today they comprehend not.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on people intoxicated with their own desires who purchase God’s wrath with their souls and wealth; the image of intoxication.

selected.text: O my Lord! The world hath occupied me from turning toward Thy horizon and hath prevented me from directing myself to the Dayspring of Thy Cause and the Dawning-Place of Thy Revelation. Therefore have I fled from myself unto Thee and have placed my trust in Thee.
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh in the voice of one whom the world has kept from God’s horizon and who flees from self to Him; makes the examination personal.

selected.text: Although all testify to the transience of the world and whatsoever is therein, … nevertheless they have become so beguiled by ephemeral means that they have, on account of these, shut their eyes to the enduring divine bounties and the sublime, transcendent stations
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that though all testify to the world’s transience they shut their eyes to enduring bounties; continues the gap between knowing and choosing.

selected.text: There is a vast difference between the soul who has consecrated his life to the joys, pleasures and delights of this mundane world and the soul who seeks nought else save the good-pleasure of the Lord, who devotes his rest and comfort to the progress of the Cause.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting a life consecrated to pleasures with one devoting its rest and comfort to the progress of the Cause; comfort and purposeful service.

selected.text: However, there are some cities whose residents are so deeply absorbed in the world of nature that they are wholly bereft of spiritual perception. They occupy themselves with eating, resting, dancing and amusement. They are entirely unaware of the kingdom of heaven.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on city dwellers so absorbed in nature that they occupy themselves with eating, dancing and amusement; diagnosis in a social setting.

selected.text: Affairs have so transformed that thou seest vultures dwelling in palaces while the Sovereign of the Kingdom resideth in the most ruined of houses. Thus hath the matter been decreed by thy Lord, the Mighty, the Self-Subsisting. God hath made their palaces their tombs.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh on vultures dwelling in palaces and God making their palaces their tombs; the movement from palaces to tombs.

selected.text: and loved Him would sacrifice his soul in His path and would pay no heed to the worlds, for beyond this world there exists a kingdom and a mighty sovereignty, and worlds which none can reckon save the Self of thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. Grieve not over your bodies, for We have desired that ye should possess the kingdoms of the spirit
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that beyond this world lie spiritual kingdoms, so grieve not over your bodies; widens the horizon of loss.

selected.text: Ere this she was a captive in the fetters of material attachments; now she is established upon the throne of joy. Ere this she was a prisoner in the bond of this ephemeral world; now, like unto the birds of holiness, she hath winged her flight unto the realm of freedom.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá remembering a departed woman once captive in material fetters and now flown like the birds of holiness to freedom; release seen at death.

selected.text: They whose eyes have been opened behold this world and its ornaments as a mirage which the thirsty one thinketh to be water. They are indeed possessed of insight. Nothing can prevent them from the Most Great Vision. They shall soon find themselves in an exalted station.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that those with opened eyes see the world and its ornaments as a mirage; the mirage image as insight.

selected.text: Every youth in this earthly realm is preoccupied with thoughts of this world and immersed in animal passions. Their thoughts are of food and drink, their pursuits the desire for pearls and shells, even the basest clay fragments. But the end result is regret and remorse.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on youth preoccupied with food, drink and shells, ending in regret; desire in youth.

selected.text: We summon the people to severance and enkindlement. We call their attention to spirituality. We have nothing to do with political tricks and chicaneries. All the nations and governments of the world are harbouring these thoughts, are flying in this devitalizing atmosphere.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá summoning people to severance and spirituality, apart from political chicanery; detachment from politics.

selected.text: And how can one who sees no life for himself in less than a moment desire the world? How strange that those who speak according to their own desires - they shall be questioned about what they have said on that Day when they shall find for themselves no helper or assistant.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how one who sees no life for himself beyond a moment can desire the world; mortality and desire.

selected.text: Days pass by and one's life span comes to an end and no condition remains the same but there is a difference between the soul who passes his days in selfish desires and lusts and one who consecrates the duration of his life in suffering in the path of the lord of revelation.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting a life of selfish desire with one consecrated to suffering in God’s path; the difference a life’s direction makes.

selected.text: Your room will have no worldly comforts, but will be filled with the love of God. During a terrible storm Christ wandered on the mountain seeking shelter; a den of wild beasts was all he found and that was the beloved Son of God. All the world was his, but no worldly riches.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Christ, to whom all the world belonged, found only a den for shelter; an example of poverty and love.

selected.text: They are heedless of being inflicted with a myriad of spiritual catastrophes, but do not desire the least harm to come to this transient body or be exposed to any jeopardy. They say whatever may happen to our soul, let it happen; but nothing less than utmost comfort for our body!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on people who accept spiritual catastrophe but demand utmost comfort for the body; a vivid inversion of priorities.

selected.text: All human beings are earthly; their hearts are connected with this world. Day and night their thoughts and occupations are earthly; all belong to this world. They think about the honors of this world, or about the riches and wealth of this world, or of name and fame in this world.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that all human beings are earthly, thinking of honors, riches and fame; a general diagnosis.

selected.text: O people! Turn not unto the world and its ornaments. By God! It shall perish, and ye shall return to an abode wherein ye shall find no companion for yourselves. Hearken unto My words and deprive not yourselves of meeting your Lord, and be not among the rebellious in the land.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh: turn not to the world, it shall perish and ye shall return to an abode without companion; a warning of solitude.

selected.text: The love of the world hath prevented and deprived the peoples from turning to the Ancient Beauty, exalted be His glory. We beseech Him to bestow upon thee a strength which no weakness can affect, that perchance the light of certitude may triumph over the darkness of vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praying that certitude may triumph over vain imaginings where love of the world has deprived the peoples; strength amid confusion.

selected.text: As for the unfaithful, they forgot the Abha Beauty to such an extent that each became occupied with their own comfort, ease and pleasure. One fell into thoughts of fame, another into delusions of glory. One sought peace of soul while another pursued the desires of heart and spirit.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the unfaithful who forgot the Abha Beauty in comfort, fame and glory; worldliness after faith.

selected.text: Although their armies ride forth in battle and they call themselves victorious and conquer countries and nations on every side they are already vanquished by their own egos, they are all captives of self and desire. Thus are they laid low in truth and humiliated like powerless slaves
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that outward conquerors are already vanquished by their own egos; shows captivity behind victory.

selected.text: Now consider them, and consider those others who will not forego one iota of their lusts and passions. Slaves are they of their carnal appetites, and addicted to the pleasures and diversions of this dark and narrow world. Wherefore is there an immeasurable difference betwixt the twain.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on slaves of carnal appetite in this dark narrow world and the immeasurable difference from the detached; contrasting lives.

selected.text: If he could spread such a banquet of rejoicing for me, he could do it for himself a hundred times better. Notwithstanding this ideal power, he is still walking in the wilderness, eating the grass, sleeping on the ground, sitting in the darkness and living altogether a life of poverty
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on one who could spread a banquet yet lives in poverty in the wilderness; a narrative of chosen simplicity.

selected.text: The similitude of the world is as a shadow - at times it existeth and at times it existeth not. No wise one would attach their heart to such a thing, but rather would consider it vain. … Think not that the world and what is meant by it are the ordained bounties therein or its varied ornaments
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh likening the world to a shadow and denying that the world means the ordained bounties and ornaments within it; carries the introduction’s distinction about created bounties.

selected.text: Yazid too departed this world, and the Lord of the Martyrs likewise departed this world - what a difference between them! That one passed his days in passion and desire, in tyranny and transgression; this one spent all his days in the path of God, carrying them to their ultimate conclusion.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting Yazid’s life of passion with the Lord of the Martyrs’ life in God’s path; a narrative contrast of two deaths.

selected.text: The ornaments of the world have occupied the peoples and kept them back from the recognition of God, exalted be His glory. By ornaments is meant at times the love of the world, and at other times its trappings and adornments, and in one station all that preventeth men from drawing nigh unto God.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh distinguishing the several meanings of the world’s ornaments, from love of the world to all that prevents nearness to God; clarifies the meanings of worldliness.

selected.text: abandon the world and whatsoever is therein and thereon of its customs and creeds, for all these are one and the same in judgment … For whatsoever veils man from the recognition of his Lord and from attaining the presence of his Master - this is the world, even though it be the most excellent of deeds
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh that whatever veils one from recognizing his Lord is the world, even the most excellent of deeds; carries the introduction’s claim about an apparently excellent deed.

selected.text: Some men’s lives are solely occupied with the things of this world; their minds are so circumscribed by exterior manners and traditional interests that they are blind to any other realm of existence, to the spiritual significance of all things! They think and dream of earthly fame, of material progress
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: There are many assemblies throughout the world. In every city there are assemblies in perfect order, but all are connected to the material world. One assembly is for amassing riches, another for seizing people's wealth, another for discovering mines and inventing tools and instruments as time passes, and so forth.
